videos.script: The stock of one book is a hundred copies. A sale of two arrives, and the database says ninety-eight. {{sale}} Then the consumer crashes before it tells Kafka it is done. It starts again, and the same sale arrives again. Ninety-six. {{again}} Nobody bought those two copies. The website now says ninety-six, and the shelf has ninety-eight. {{shelf}} Kafka promised at least once, and it kept its promise. The duplicate is not a bug in Kafka. It is the price of not losing anything. {{price}} So the database has to pay it. {{pay}} There are three ways. Write values that come out the same however often they are written. Remember which sales you have already applied. Or keep your place in the stream inside the database, in the same transaction as the stock. {{three}} In this lesson the stock lives in SQLite, and you feed it the same sales twice. The point is to see the numbers stay where they were. {{same}}
